Very nice lunch
Jun 2018 • Friends
We came here for lunch on our very first day in Hanoi, having flown in earlier and had a very brief view of Hanoi from the airport.
It was a set menu lunch and we were only a tiny bit surprised to meet up with a similar group that we met earlier in the hotel in Hue, obviously doing the same route as us and in the same direction too!
Anyway. The staff were very friendly, the seating arrangements worked fine, the overall decor of the building and the inside was in the old French colonial style.
We did not have a long wait for lunch and we had already had the set menu chosen for us by our national guide.
it was a very nice mixture of seafood, chicken and pork, with vegetables, rice and spring roll. We also had a small bowl of soup.
The food was a very decent temperature, very fresh and very tasty. They catered very well too for a couple of our guests who ate vegetarian.
Very happy with the clean, tasty meal, and the nice ambience about the place.

Disappointing tiger prawns
Apr 2017 • Couples
Ordered the prawns in claypot. Was informed some minutes after the order was taken that they weren't available. Upon making my next choice I was then informed I could have them again (we think the chef had returned as we saw a young man come back inside). In the end I wished they hadn't become available as they came out rubbery. One of the 6 looked mutated and by the time it was peeled was less than 2 cm in size and shriveled so I left it as by then my appetite had passed. The sauce was tangy but didn't compensate for the lack lustre prawns. When I asked the waitress for a serviette to wipe my hands of the sticky sauce she could not offer any and suggested I went to the bathroom. Whilst this was no issue I found it rather strange, since when ordering prawns from other places where peeling of shells is required I've always received a bowl of water to rinse at the table. There appeared to be serviettes at some other tables just not ours. Perhaps she misunderstood? 
My husband was fairly satisfied with the pork ribs so if you want to eat here maybe just avoid the prawns. 
Unfortunately a disappointing experience for our 2nd night in Hanoi.

A Delicious Buffet for Families or Groups by Didier Corlou
Dec 2016 • Friends
I think this restaurant has a simple premise:
Serve traditional street-food dishes of Hanoi...without the street

This is probably the best restaurant to take your out-of-town friends and family to who really want to try all the local favorites...but don't want the noise, discomfort, and questionable sanitation of the street or small vendors.

Food
Traditionally made Vietnamese...just executed better than 99% of the street or small-shop vendors. Truly, the Pho, Banh Cuon and grilled meats are very good. I imagine this is what the original (and long-past) Quan-Ngon might have been created to be. A great place to try all the standards as they were meant to be done. The non-Vietnamese food was OK, but unimpressive and seemed more like an after-thought aimed at appealing to a local crowd.

Service
Attentive in a way you miss in Hanoi and yet not suffocating. Although I admit that one quiet evening we had a waitress hover a little close until the manager stepped in to have her relocate a bit further off.

Atmosphere
It's good. I like the old French villa setting and sitting outside is great when the weather's nice (similar to the original Madame Hien). The interior is tasteful and not crowded but can feel a bit quiet when it's empty and a bit loud when it's full (similar to the original Madame Hien).

I'm not usually a fan of buffets but Corlou has got this one right. With the closure of a buffet on Nguyen Thai Hoc (the name escapes me), I'd vote for Madame Hien Buffet as the top Vietnamese buffet in town.

Other:
The lunch buffet is cheaper but omits the grilled meats. Go for dinner.
The bottled beer options are a little thin and rather expensive.
The wine by the glass was good and moderately priced.
It seems like DC hasn't done a great job defining this restaurant. While I think it's a great place for out-of-towners seeking traditional VN food, it seems like it's targeted more at locals and ex-pats. Really, of all of DC's restaurants* this is the one which feels a little lacking in vision.

*I should mention that I haven't had an opportunity to have dinner at La Verticale yet. If you're searching for a present...I'd enjoy a gift certificate!

Lovely experience
Dec 2016 • Family
This is their second (and newer) location and it was a great dining experience. Attentive and pleasant service crew, led by an equally hands-on manager who not only served but made the rice rolls. We opted for their buffet and there were a couple of open-kitchen stations to watch the food preparation process. The food is also presented in small quantities on the buffet table and is constantly topped up for freshness. Both my kids enjoyed themselves, and the staff were attentive to their needs, taking time to chat with them. We will certainly return the next time we visit Hanoi.
